LEV.P.8.1-13.text: Moses Consecrates Aaron and His Sons

LEV.P.10.1-7.text: The Sin of Nadab and Abihu

LEV.P.23.4-8.text: Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread

LEV.1.1-2.text: The LORD speaks to Moses about animal offerings

LEV.1.3-4.text: An Israelite brings a bull as a burnt offering

LEV.1.5-6.text: The bull is killed and the priests sprinkle its blood

LEV.1.7-9.text: Priests burn the pieces of the bull on the altar

LEV.1.10-11.text: A sheep or goat may be a burnt offering

LEV.1.12-13.text: The priest burns the pieces of the sheep or goat

LEV.1.14-15.text: A bird may be given as a burnt offering

LEV.1.16-17.text: The priest prepares the bird and burns it on the altar

LEV.2.1-3.text: A grain offering is fine flour with oil and frankincense

LEV.2.4-5.text: Grain offerings baked in an oven or cooked on a griddle

LEV.2.6-7.text: Grain offerings may also be cooked in a pan

LEV.2.8-10.text: The priest burns a part; the rest is for Aaron’s sons

LEV.2.11-13.text: Grain offerings must have no leaven or honey, but salt

LEV.2.14-16.text: Israelites offer roasted new grain as firstfruits

LEV.3.1-2.text: An Israelite brings a bull or cow as a peace offering

LEV.3.3-5.text: The priests burn the fat of the peace offering

LEV.3.6-8.text: A peace offering may come from the flock

LEV.3.9-11.text: The priest burns the fat of the lamb on the altar

LEV.3.12-14.text: A goat may also be given as a peace offering

LEV.3.15-17.text: The LORD forbids Israelites to eat fat or blood

LEV.4.1-3.text: A priest who sins must bring a young bull

LEV.4.4-5.text: The priest kills the bull and takes blood into the Tent

LEV.4.6-7.text: The priest sprinkles blood and puts it on the altar horns

LEV.4.8-10.text: The priest burns the fat of the sin offering bull

LEV.4.11-12.text: The rest of the bull is burned outside the camp

LEV.4.13-15.text: If all Israel sins by mistake, the elders offer a bull

LEV.4.16-17.text: The priest sprinkles the bull’s blood before the veil

LEV.4.18-19.text: The priest puts blood on the altar and burns the fat

LEV.4.20-21.text: The priest burns the bull and the people are forgiven

LEV.4.22-23.text: A leader who sins must bring a male goat

LEV.4.24-25.text: The leader’s goat is killed and its blood put on the altar

LEV.4.26-26.text: The priest burns the goat’s fat and the leader is forgiven

LEV.4.27-28.text: A common person who sins must bring a female goat

LEV.4.29-30.text: The female goat is killed and its blood put on the altar

LEV.4.31-31.text: The priest burns the fat and the sinner is forgiven

LEV.4.32-33.text: A sinner may bring a female lamb without fault

LEV.4.34-35.text: The priest offers the lamb’s blood and fat for forgiveness

LEV.5.1-2.text: A person sins by not testifying or touching unclean things

LEV.5.3-4.text: A person is guilty for human uncleanness or a rash oath

LEV.5.5-6.text: A guilty person must confess and bring a lamb or goat

LEV.5.7-9.text: A person who cannot afford a lamb may bring two birds

LEV.5.10-10.text: The priest offers the second bird as a burnt offering

LEV.5.11-11.text: A very poor person may bring fine flour as a sin offering

LEV.5.12-13.text: The priest burns a handful of flour for forgiveness

LEV.5.14-16.text: Someone who sins against holy things must bring a ram

LEV.5.17-19.text: A person who sins without knowing it still brings a ram

LEV.6.1-4.text: A person who cheats a neighbor must give back what he took

LEV.6.5-7.text: The cheater repays in full, adds a fifth, and brings a ram

LEV.6.8-9.text: The priests keep the burnt offering on the altar all night

LEV.6.10-11.text: A priest carries the altar ashes outside the camp

LEV.6.12-13.text: The priests must never let the altar fire go out

LEV.6.14-15.text: Priests burn a handful of the grain offering

LEV.6.16-18.text: Aaron’s sons eat the rest of the grain offering

LEV.6.19-20.text: Aaron and his sons bring flour as a regular offering

LEV.6.21-23.text: A priest’s grain offering must be burned completely

LEV.6.24-26.text: The priest eats the sin offering in a holy place

LEV.6.27-28.text: Priests must wash stained clothes and clean the pots

LEV.6.29-30.text: Male priests eat most sin offerings; some are burned

LEV.7.1-4.text: Priests offer the fat of the guilt offering

LEV.7.5-6.text: Male priests eat the guilt offering in a holy place

LEV.7.7-8.text: The guilt offering and sin offering have the same law

LEV.7.9-10.text: Cooked grain offerings belong to the priests

LEV.7.11-12.text: A thanksgiving peace offering needs cakes without yeast

LEV.7.13-14.text: A person giving thanks also brings leavened bread

LEV.7.15-16.text: A thanksgiving offering must be eaten the same day

LEV.7.17-18.text: Peace offering meat left until the third day must be burned

LEV.7.19-20.text: Unclean people must not eat the peace offering meat

LEV.7.21-21.text: Anyone unclean who eats the peace offering is cut off

LEV.7.22-24.text: The Israelites must not eat the fat of ox, sheep or goat

LEV.7.25-27.text: Israelites must not eat fat from offerings or any blood

LEV.7.28-30.text: Israelites bring peace offerings and wave the breast

LEV.7.31-32.text: The priests receive the breast and the right thigh

LEV.7.33-34.text: The breast and thigh are a permanent portion for priests

LEV.7.35-36.text: Aaron’s sons receive this portion for all generations

LEV.7.37-38.text: Summary of the laws for the offerings given at Sinai

LEV.8.1-3.text: The LORD tells Moses to bring Aaron and gather the people

LEV.8.4-5.text: Moses gathers the people at the Tent of Meeting

LEV.8.6-7.text: Moses washes Aaron and his sons and dresses Aaron

LEV.8.8-9.text: Moses puts the breastpiece and turban on Aaron

LEV.8.10-11.text: Moses anoints the tabernacle and the altar with oil

LEV.8.12-13.text: Moses anoints Aaron and dresses Aaron’s sons

LEV.8.14-15.text: Moses offers the bull as a sin offering

LEV.8.16-17.text: Moses burns the bull’s fat and the rest outside the camp

LEV.8.18-19.text: Moses offers a ram as a burnt offering

LEV.8.20-21.text: Moses burns the whole ram on the altar

LEV.8.22-24.text: Moses puts blood from the ordination ram on the priests

LEV.8.25-27.text: Moses waves the fat, thigh and bread before the LORD

LEV.8.28-29.text: Moses burns the offerings and waves the breast

LEV.8.30-30.text: Moses sprinkles oil and blood on Aaron and his sons

LEV.8.31-33.text: Moses tells the priests to boil and eat the meat

LEV.8.34-36.text: Aaron and his sons must stay at the Tent seven days

LEV.9.1-2.text: Moses tells Aaron to bring a bull and a ram

LEV.9.3-5.text: Moses tells the Israelites to bring offerings

LEV.9.6-7.text: Aaron must offer sacrifices for himself and the people

LEV.9.8-9.text: Aaron offers a sin offering for himself

LEV.9.10-11.text: Aaron burns the sin offering fat and the flesh

LEV.9.12-14.text: Aaron offers the burnt offering on the altar

LEV.9.15-17.text: Aaron offers the people’s sin, burnt and grain offerings

LEV.9.18-19.text: Aaron offers the people’s peace offering

LEV.9.20-21.text: Aaron burns the fat and waves the breasts and thigh

LEV.9.22-24.text: The glory of the LORD appears and fire burns the offering

LEV.10.1-2.text: Nadab and Abihu offer unauthorized fire and die

LEV.10.3-4.text: Aaron is silent; Moses has the bodies carried out of camp

LEV.10.5-7.text: Moses forbids Aaron and his sons to mourn openly

LEV.10.8-11.text: Priests must not drink wine in the Tent of Meeting

LEV.10.12-13.text: Moses tells Aaron’s sons to eat the grain offering

LEV.10.14-15.text: Aaron’s family may eat the wave offering breast and thigh

LEV.10.16-18.text: Moses is angry that the sin offering was not eaten

LEV.10.19-20.text: Aaron explains and Moses is satisfied

LEV.11.1-2.text: The LORD tells Moses and Aaron about animals to eat

LEV.11.3-4.text: Animals with split hooves that chew the cud may be eaten

LEV.11.5-8.text: The rock badger, rabbit and pig are unclean

LEV.11.9-10.text: Only water creatures with fins and scales may be eaten

LEV.11.11-12.text: Water creatures without fins and scales are detestable

LEV.11.13-16.text: Eagles, vultures, ravens and other birds must not be eaten

LEV.11.17-19.text: Owls, herons, bats and other birds must not be eaten

LEV.11.20-23.text: Locusts and crickets may be eaten; other insects may not

LEV.11.24-25.text: Touching a dead unclean animal makes a person unclean

LEV.11.26-28.text: Touching more dead unclean animals makes a person unclean

LEV.11.29-30.text: Moles, mice and lizards are unclean

LEV.11.31-33.text: Dead crawling creatures make objects and clay pots unclean

LEV.11.34-35.text: Food, drink and ovens touched by a carcass become unclean

LEV.11.36-38.text: Water in springs stays clean; wet seed can become unclean

LEV.11.39-40.text: Touching or eating an animal that died makes one unclean

LEV.11.41-42.text: Israelites must not eat creatures that crawl on the ground

LEV.11.43-45.text: The LORD tells Israelites to be holy because he is holy

LEV.11.46-47.text: Summary of the law about clean and unclean animals

LEV.12.1-3.text: A woman who bears a son is unclean seven days

LEV.12.4-5.text: A mother’s purification lasts longer after a daughter

LEV.12.6-6.text: A mother brings a lamb and a bird to the priest

LEV.12.7-8.text: The priest makes the mother clean; poor women bring birds

LEV.13.1-2.text: A person with a swelling or rash must go to the priest

LEV.13.3-4.text: The priest examines a sore and may isolate the person

LEV.13.5-6.text: If the sore fades, the priest declares the person clean

LEV.13.7-8.text: If the rash spreads, the priest declares the person unclean

LEV.13.9-11.text: A chronic skin disease makes the person unclean

LEV.13.12-14.text: A person is clean if the disease turns all skin white

LEV.13.15-17.text: Raw flesh is unclean, but flesh that turns white is clean

LEV.13.18-20.text: The priest examines a healed boil that has a white spot

LEV.13.21-23.text: The priest waits seven days to see if a boil spot spreads

LEV.13.24-25.text: A burn with white hair and deep skin is unclean

LEV.13.26-28.text: The priest checks a burn spot again after seven days

LEV.13.29-30.text: A scaly infection on the head or chin is unclean

LEV.13.31-31.text: The priest isolates a person with a shallow scaly sore

LEV.13.32-33.text: A person shaves around the scaly area and waits seven days

LEV.13.34-34.text: The priest declares the person clean after seven days

LEV.13.35-37.text: A spreading scaly sore is unclean; a healed one is clean

LEV.13.38-39.text: Dull white spots on the skin are harmless and clean

LEV.13.40-41.text: A man who is bald is still clean

LEV.13.42-44.text: A reddish-white sore on a bald head is unclean

LEV.13.45-46.text: A person with a skin disease must live outside the camp

LEV.13.47-49.text: Mildew in cloth or leather must be shown to the priest

LEV.13.50-52.text: Cloth with spreading mildew must be burned

LEV.13.53-55.text: Washed cloth that has not changed must be burned

LEV.13.56-58.text: Faded mildew is cut out; returning mildew is burned

LEV.13.59-59.text: This is the law about mildew in cloth and leather

LEV.14.1-2.text: The LORD tells Moses how to cleanse a healed person

LEV.14.3-5.text: The priest checks the healed person and gets two birds

LEV.14.6-7.text: The priest sprinkles the person and frees the live bird

LEV.14.8-9.text: The healed person washes, shaves, and waits seven days

LEV.14.10-11.text: On day eight the person brings lambs, flour, and oil

LEV.14.12-13.text: The priest offers one lamb as a guilt offering

LEV.14.14-16.text: The priest puts blood on the person’s ear, thumb, and toe

LEV.14.17-18.text: The priest puts oil on the ear, thumb, toe, and head

LEV.14.19-20.text: The priest offers the sin offering and the burnt offering

LEV.14.21-23.text: A poor person may bring one lamb and two birds

LEV.14.24-25.text: The priest offers the lamb and puts blood on the person

LEV.14.26-27.text: The priest sprinkles oil seven times before the LORD

LEV.14.28-29.text: The priest puts oil on the person and makes atonement

LEV.14.30-32.text: This is the law for a poor person with skin disease

LEV.14.33-35.text: A house owner must tell the priest about mildew

LEV.14.36-38.text: The priest inspects the house and closes it seven days

LEV.14.39-40.text: If the mildew spreads, the priest removes the stones

LEV.14.41-42.text: The house is scraped and new stones and plaster are used

LEV.14.43-44.text: If mildew returns, the priest declares the house unclean

LEV.14.45-47.text: A house with bad mildew must be torn down

LEV.14.48-48.text: The priest declares the house clean if mildew is gone

LEV.14.49-51.text: The priest uses two birds to purify the house

LEV.14.52-53.text: The priest releases the live bird and the house is clean

LEV.14.54-57.text: Summary of the laws about skin diseases and mildew

LEV.15.1-3.text: A man with a bodily discharge is unclean

LEV.15.4-5.text: Beds and seats of a man with a discharge are unclean

LEV.15.6-7.text: Touching the man or his seat makes a person unclean

LEV.15.8-9.text: The man’s spit and saddle cause uncleanness

LEV.15.10-12.text: More rules about touching the man and what he touched

LEV.15.13-15.text: A man healed of a discharge washes and brings offerings

LEV.15.16-18.text: A man with an emission of semen must bathe

LEV.15.19-20.text: A woman’s monthly period makes her unclean seven days

LEV.15.21-23.text: Touching a woman’s bed or seat makes a person unclean

LEV.15.24-24.text: A man who lies with a woman in her period is unclean

LEV.15.25-27.text: A woman with a long bleeding is unclean

LEV.15.28-30.text: A woman healed of her discharge brings offerings

LEV.15.31-31.text: The Israelites must be kept from uncleanness

LEV.15.32-33.text: Summary of the laws about discharges

LEV.16.1-2.text: The LORD tells Aaron not to enter freely behind the veil

LEV.16.3-5.text: Aaron must bring offerings and wear holy clothes

LEV.16.6-7.text: Aaron offers a bull for himself and presents two goats

LEV.16.8-10.text: Aaron chooses one goat for the LORD and one to send away

LEV.16.11-11.text: Aaron slaughters the bull as his own sin offering

LEV.16.12-13.text: Aaron brings burning coals and incense behind the veil

LEV.16.14-14.text: Aaron sprinkles the bull’s blood at the mercy seat

LEV.16.15-16.text: Aaron uses the goat’s blood to cleanse the Most Holy Place

LEV.16.17-19.text: Aaron cleanses the altar with blood from both animals

LEV.16.20-22.text: Aaron puts the people’s sins on the live goat

LEV.16.23-24.text: Aaron changes his clothes and offers burnt offerings

LEV.16.25-26.text: Aaron burns the fat; the man with the goat must wash

LEV.16.27-28.text: The sin offering animals are burned outside the camp

LEV.16.29-31.text: The Israelites must rest and humble themselves each year

LEV.16.32-33.text: Future high priests make atonement for the people

LEV.16.34-34.text: Atonement for Israel is to be made once a year

LEV.17.1-4.text: Israelites must bring animals to the Tent of Meeting

LEV.17.5-6.text: Israelites must bring field sacrifices to the priest

LEV.17.7-7.text: Israelites must stop offering sacrifices to goat demons

LEV.17.8-9.text: Israelites and foreigners must bring offerings to the Tent

LEV.17.10-11.text: Eating blood is forbidden because blood makes atonement

LEV.17.12-13.text: No one may eat blood; hunters must cover it with dirt

LEV.17.14-14.text: Israelites must not eat the blood of any creature

LEV.17.15-16.text: Anyone who eats a dead animal must wash and bathe

LEV.18.1-3.text: Israelites must not copy the customs of Egypt or Canaan

LEV.18.4-5.text: Israelites must obey the LORD’s laws and so live

LEV.18.6-8.text: Israelites must not have sex with mother or stepmother

LEV.18.9-11.text: Israelites must not have sex with sisters or granddaughters

LEV.18.12-14.text: Men must not have sex with an aunt or uncle’s wife

LEV.18.15-16.text: Israelites must not have sex with a son’s or brother’s wife

LEV.18.17-18.text: Men must not have sex with a wife’s daughter or sister

LEV.18.19-20.text: Men must avoid sex in a period or with a neighbor’s wife

LEV.18.21-21.text: Israelites must not give children as sacrifices to Molech

LEV.18.22-23.text: Sex between men and sex with animals are forbidden

LEV.18.24-25.text: Israelites must not defile themselves as the nations did

LEV.18.26-28.text: Israelites and foreigners must not do these evil acts

LEV.18.29-30.text: Those who do these acts must be cut off from Israel

LEV.19.1-4.text: Israelites must be holy, honor parents and avoid idols

LEV.19.5-8.text: Israelites must eat peace offerings within two days

LEV.19.9-10.text: Israelites must leave extra harvest for the poor

LEV.19.11-12.text: Israelites must not steal, lie or swear falsely

LEV.19.13-14.text: Israelites must be fair to workers, the deaf and the blind

LEV.19.15-16.text: Israelites must judge fairly and not spread slander

LEV.19.17-18.text: Israelites must not hate or take revenge but love neighbors

LEV.19.19-19.text: God tells Israel not to mix animals, seeds, or cloth

LEV.19.20-22.text: A man who lies with a promised slave girl brings a ram

LEV.19.23-25.text: Israel must not eat fruit from new trees for three years

LEV.19.26-28.text: God forbids eating blood, sorcery, and cutting hair or skin

LEV.19.29-30.text: Israel must not prostitute daughters and must keep Sabbaths

LEV.19.31-31.text: Israel must not turn to mediums or spiritists

LEV.19.32-32.text: Israel must honor the elderly and fear God

LEV.19.33-34.text: Israel must love foreigners as native-born citizens

LEV.19.35-37.text: Israel must use honest scales and keep all God’s laws

LEV.20.1-2.text: Anyone who gives a child to Molech must be put to death

LEV.20.3-5.text: God will cut off those who give children to Molech

LEV.20.6-7.text: God will cut off anyone who turns to mediums

LEV.20.8-9.text: Israel must keep God’s laws; cursing parents brings death

LEV.20.10-12.text: Death is the punishment for adultery and sex with relatives

LEV.20.13-14.text: Punishment for a man who lies with a man

LEV.20.15-16.text: People who lie with animals must die, and the animals too

LEV.20.17-18.text: Punishment for sex with a sister or a menstruating woman

LEV.20.19-21.text: Sex with an aunt or a relative’s wife brings punishment

LEV.20.22-23.text: Israel must keep God’s laws, not follow other nations

LEV.20.24-25.text: God sets Israel apart; Israel must avoid unclean animals

LEV.20.26-26.text: Israel must be holy because God is holy

LEV.20.27-27.text: Mediums and spiritists must be put to death

LEV.21.1-3.text: A priest may touch the dead only for close family

LEV.21.4-6.text: Priests must be holy and not shave or cut themselves

LEV.21.7-9.text: A priest must not marry a prostitute or divorced woman

LEV.21.10-12.text: The high priest must not touch any dead body

LEV.21.13-15.text: The high priest must marry a virgin from his own people

LEV.21.16-17.text: No descendant of Aaron with a defect may offer God’s food

LEV.21.18-21.text: Aaron’s descendants with defects must not present offerings

LEV.21.22-24.text: Priests with defects eat holy food but stay away from altar

LEV.22.1-3.text: Aaron and his sons must respect the sacred offerings

LEV.22.4-6.text: Unclean priests may not eat the sacred offerings

LEV.22.7-9.text: Priests become clean at sunset and then may eat offerings

LEV.22.10-11.text: Who in a priest’s household may eat the sacred offering

LEV.22.12-13.text: When a priest’s daughter may eat the sacred food

LEV.22.14-16.text: A person who eats a sacred offering by mistake must repay

LEV.22.17-19.text: Burnt offerings must be unblemished male animals

LEV.22.20-21.text: Peace offerings must also have no defect

LEV.22.22-23.text: Israelites must not offer blind, injured or sick animals

LEV.22.24-25.text: Israelites must not offer animals with damaged testicles

LEV.22.26-27.text: A young animal must stay with its mother seven days

LEV.22.28-30.text: Israelites must eat a thank offering on the same day

LEV.22.31-33.text: Israelites must obey the LORD and keep his name holy

LEV.23.1-2.text: The LORD tells Moses about his appointed feasts

LEV.23.3-3.text: Israelites must rest on the Sabbath day

LEV.23.4-6.text: Israelites keep Passover and eat unleavened bread

LEV.23.7-8.text: Israelites must not work on the first and seventh days

LEV.23.9-11.text: Israelites bring the first grain sheaf to the priest

LEV.23.12-14.text: Israelites give offerings before eating the new grain

LEV.23.15-16.text: Israelites count seven weeks, then offer new grain

LEV.23.17-18.text: Israelites bring two loaves and animals as offerings

LEV.23.19-21.text: Israelites offer a goat and lambs and hold an assembly

LEV.23.22-22.text: Israelites must leave some harvest for the poor

LEV.23.26-27.text: Israelites hold a sacred assembly and bring an offering

LEV.23.28-29.text: Israelites must not work on the Day of Atonement

LEV.23.30-32.text: Israelites keep a full rest from evening to evening

LEV.23.33-34.text: The feast begins on the fifteenth day of the seventh month

LEV.23.35-36.text: Israelites hold assemblies on the first and eighth days

LEV.23.37-38.text: Israelites bring set offerings on each feast day

LEV.23.39-39.text: Israelites celebrate a feast after gathering the harvest

LEV.23.40-41.text: Israelites gather branches and rejoice before the LORD

LEV.23.42-44.text: Israelites live in booths to remember leaving Egypt

LEV.24.1-2.text: Israelites bring pure olive oil for the lamps

LEV.24.3-4.text: Aaron must tend the lamps every night before the LORD

LEV.24.5-6.text: Israelites bake twelve loaves for the gold table

LEV.24.7-9.text: Aaron and his sons eat the bread each Sabbath

LEV.24.10-12.text: A man curses the LORD’s name and is put in custody

LEV.24.13-14.text: The LORD orders that the blasphemer be stoned

LEV.24.15-16.text: Anyone who curses God’s name must die, foreigner or native

LEV.24.17-18.text: Killing a man means death; killing an animal means repaying

LEV.24.19-21.text: Injuries are repaid in the same way: eye for eye

LEV.24.22-23.text: One law for all; the Israelites stone the blasphemer

LEV.25.1-2.text: The LORD tells Moses the land must keep a Sabbath

LEV.25.3-4.text: The land rests from farming in the seventh year

LEV.25.5-7.text: In the seventh year all may eat what the land grows

LEV.25.8-9.text: The Israelites count forty-nine years and sound the horn

LEV.25.10-10.text: The fiftieth year brings liberty and return to property

LEV.25.11-12.text: In the Jubilee year the Israelites must not sow or reap

LEV.25.13-14.text: Israelites must not cheat each other in buying and selling

LEV.25.15-17.text: Land prices depend on the years left until the Jubilee

LEV.25.18-19.text: Obeying God’s laws brings safety and plenty in the land

LEV.25.20-22.text: God promises a sixth-year crop big enough for three years

LEV.25.23-25.text: The land belongs to God; a relative may redeem sold land

LEV.25.26-28.text: A man may redeem his sold land or get it back at Jubilee

LEV.25.29-30.text: A house in a walled city can be redeemed for one year

LEV.25.31-32.text: Village houses can be redeemed; Levites may always redeem

LEV.25.33-34.text: Levite houses return at Jubilee; pastureland is never sold

LEV.25.39-41.text: A poor Israelite who sells himself is not made a slave

LEV.25.42-44.text: Israelites are God’s servants and must not be slaves

LEV.25.45-46.text: Israelites may own foreign slaves, not rule brothers harshly

LEV.25.47-48.text: An Israelite sold to a foreigner may be redeemed

LEV.25.49-50.text: A relative or the man himself may pay for his redemption

LEV.25.51-52.text: The price of redemption depends on the years until Jubilee

LEV.25.53-55.text: An Israelite servant goes free in the Year of Jubilee

LEV.26.1-2.text: The Israelites must not make idols and must keep Sabbaths

LEV.26.3-4.text: God promises rain and good crops if Israelites obey

LEV.26.5-6.text: God promises plenty of food, peace and safety in the land

LEV.26.7-8.text: God promises the Israelites victory over enemies

LEV.26.9-10.text: God promises many children and his covenant with Israel

LEV.26.11-13.text: God promises to live among the Israelites

LEV.26.14-15.text: God warns Israel about refusing to obey his commands

LEV.26.16-17.text: God warns of terror, disease and defeat by enemies

LEV.26.18-20.text: God warns of seven times more punishment and no harvest

LEV.26.21-22.text: God warns of plagues and wild animals

LEV.26.23-24.text: God will strike Israel seven times for continued hostility

LEV.26.25-26.text: God warns of war, plague and hunger

LEV.26.27-28.text: God will punish Israel in fury, seven times for sins

LEV.26.29-30.text: God will destroy the high places and despise Israel

LEV.26.31-33.text: God will ruin the cities and scatter Israel among nations

LEV.26.34-36.text: The land will rest while Israel lives among enemies

LEV.26.37-39.text: Israel will flee in fear and perish among enemies

LEV.26.40-42.text: God will remember his covenant if Israel confesses sin

LEV.26.43-43.text: Israel will pay for rejecting God’s laws

LEV.26.44-45.text: God will not destroy Israel and will keep his covenant

LEV.26.46-46.text: These are the laws God gave through Moses at Sinai

LEV.27.1-2.text: The LORD tells Moses about vows involving people

LEV.27.3-4.text: Values for vows of men and women aged 20 to 60

LEV.27.5-6.text: Values for vows of people under 20 years old

LEV.27.7-8.text: Values for people over 60 and for the poor

LEV.27.9-10.text: An animal vowed to the LORD is holy and cannot be changed

LEV.27.11-13.text: The priest values a vowed unclean animal

LEV.27.14-15.text: A man may give his house to the LORD and redeem it

LEV.27.16-16.text: The value of a field is set by the seed it needs

LEV.27.17-18.text: The field’s value depends on the Year of Jubilee

LEV.27.19-21.text: A man may redeem his field; if not, priests get it

LEV.27.22-23.text: A man may give a field he bought to the LORD

LEV.27.24-25.text: The field returns to its original owner in Jubilee

LEV.27.26-27.text: The firstborn animals belong to the LORD already

LEV.27.28-29.text: Things set apart for destruction belong to the LORD

LEV.27.30-31.text: A tenth of the land’s produce belongs to the LORD

LEV.27.32-33.text: Every tenth animal is holy to the LORD

LEV.27.34-34.text: These are the commands the LORD gave Moses at Sinai
